name: Mensuration
intro: **Write the conservation equation before any numbers.** Volume before = volume after is the whole method for a third of this topic (§3).
Cancel π and common factors symbolically first, and check the units line — mm versus cm is where these questions are lost (§1).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cone of radius 7 and height 12 (π = 22/7).
qs.h: §1 — ⅓πr²h. Dropping the ⅓ is the standard slip.

qs.q: The total surface area of a cube of edge 5 cm is
qs.h: §1 — six faces. 125 is the volume, planted.

qs.q: A sphere of radius 6 has volume kπ. Find k.
A cylinder of radius 7 and height 10 has curved surface area (π = 22/7)
qs.h: §1 — curved surface is 2πrh; the total surface would add the two circular ends.

qs.q: A solid metallic sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into spheres of radius 2 cm. How many small spheres are formed?
qs.h: §3 — volume is conserved, and volume scales as the cube of the radius.

A cone and a cylinder have the same radius and the same height. The ratio of their volumes is
qs.h: The ⅓ is the whole answer.

qs.q: The radii of two spheres are in the ratio 2 : 3. Find the ratio of their surface areas, expressed as larger ÷ smaller.
qs.h: Surface area scales as the square of the radius, volume as the cube.
qs.s: (3/2)² = 2.25, i.e. 9 : 4. (Cubing gives 3.375 — the volume ratio, planted.)

qs.q: A cylindrical tank of radius 7 m and height 5 m is full of water. Find the volume in cubic metres (π = 22/7).

audit: confusing volume with surface area, or dropping the ⅓ in the cone (§1)
scaling volumes linearly instead of by the cube of the radius (§2, §3)
using a face diagonal where the space diagonal √(l²+b²+h²) was asked (§1)
forgetting the ⅓ when comparing a cone with a cylinder of the same radius and height (§1)
scaling a surface area by k instead of k² (§2)
